name: AgentHorizon
description: AgentHorizon is a benchmark of 1,373 human-annotated judging items recorded on production desktop applications across three operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS) and six task domains. It is built from 425 size-4 paired groups; each pair contributes one positive trajectory and one adversarial negative obtained by swapping the user instruction onto a sibling trajectory, so the negative is itself a coherent successful execution of a different instruction. The corpus is partitioned by an open-weight splitter into AgentHorizon (605 items, the headline subset) and AgentHorizon-Simple (768 items, the regression companion).
citeAs: Anonymous Authors. AgentHorizon: Evaluating Agentic Judges for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Tasks. NeurIPS 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks Track submission.

rai:dataCollection: Trajectories were recorded by paid human annotators performing real instructions on Windows, Linux, and macOS using production desktop applications across six task domains.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Four-stage human pipeline per trajectory: Annotation, Review L1, Review of mistake category, and a Second-stage review. Positives also pass a post-hoc GPT-5.4 audit. Negatives are constructed by instruction-swap within a sibling pair.
rai:annotationsPerItem: One agreed label per trajectory, after the four-stage human pipeline.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Paid annotation workforce; per-annotator demographics not collected.
rai:dataLimitations: Operating systems limited to Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Application coverage is finite (107 unique applications).
All instructions and on-screen text are in English.
AgentHorizon vs AgentHorizon-Simple partition is induced by Qwen 3.5 122B-A10B in OpenCode at k=8, threshold >= 7/8.
rai:dataBiases: Application coverage is heavier in productivity tools.
Recordings reflect annotator workflows, not end-user populations.
Negatives are conditioned on what could be plausibly swapped within a pair.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No PII about end users was collected.
Test accounts with synthetic data; no real customer records.
Screenshots were spot-audited for incidental capture of identifying information.
rai:dataUseCases: Recommended: evaluating LLM-as-a-judge on long-horizon computer-use agent trajectories.
Not recommended: training an agent policy or any task other than judging.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Intended to make automatic evaluation of computer-use agents more reliable. Risks: judges calibrated on this benchmark may inherit application-coverage and construction biases; per-mistake-type and per-bucket numbers are reported so consumers can audit slices.
wasDerivedFrom: In-house human-annotated computer-use trajectories. Not derived from any prior public dataset.
wasGeneratedBy: Trajectories: paid human annotators executing instructions on production desktop applications.
Labels and mistake types: four-stage human review pipeline with a post-hoc GPT-5.4 audit of positives.
AgentHorizon vs AgentHorizon-Simple bucket: Qwen 3.5 122B-A10B in OpenCode, k=8 rollouts, threshold >= 7/8.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Hosted on Harvard Dataverse with a persistent DOI. Draft accessible only via the Anonymous Private URL during review; on acceptance, published as v1 with an open license.
